topSignals.title: Topsoe hibernates Denmark SOEC factory, cancels US plant (May 26, 2026 — first digest coverage)
topSignals.text: Topsoe announced it will hibernate its Herning, Denmark SOEC factory after demonstrating commercial-scale manufacturing capability, and has cancelled its planned second SOEC factory in Chesterfield, Virginia. The restructuring cuts ~440 jobs and follows the termination of a 5 GW First Ammonia electrolyzer agreement (March 2026) and a 100 MW SOEC supply deal. CEO Elena Scaltritti: "slower than expected development in targeted clean hydrogen markets." Topsoe raises its operating margin guidance by narrowing focus. SOFC read: A major European SOEC player pulling back from scale-up signals the green H2 supply chain for SOFC-H2 transition is developing slower than the optimistic electrolyzer ramp implied in prior digests. Near-term SOFC on natural gas is unaffected; long-term H2-fueled LCOE scenarios should flag Western SOEC supply chain risk. (Topsoe press release; QC Intel; Fuel Cells Works)

topSignals.title: InterContinental Energy P2(H2)Node: <$48/MWh off-grid green AI compute in Asia (May 12, 2026 — first digest coverage)
topSignals.text: Australian firm ICE unveiled an integrated architecture combining 1 GW nodes (200 MW AI data center + 800 MW green H2 production) delivering 99.995% uptime and all-in power costs claimed at below $48/MWh, achieved by co-locating wind/solar, electrolysis, and data center infrastructure to share CAPEX. Targets AI hyperscalers in Asia and Australia. Not SOFC — uses PEM hydrogen — but establishes a competing off-grid power model at a claimed cost well below SOFC standalone LCOE. LCOE watch: the $48/MWh is not directly comparable (H2 revenue offsets data center power cost); see LCOE section. (ICE press release; Fuel Cells Works)

topSignals.title: EFCF Lucerne — European SOFC/SOEC conference in 10 days (June 30 – July 3)
topSignals.text: The European Fuel Cell Forum convenes in Lucerne, chaired by Dr. Subhasish Mukerjee of Ceres Power. Program covers high-temperature fuel cells, electrolysers, and hydrogen; expected presentations from Elcogen (E3000 G2 commercial rollout data), Sunfire (pressurized stacks), SolydEra, academic MS-SOFC research, and Topsoe (post-restructuring positioning). Watch for new stack efficiency records, degradation benchmarks, and supply chain announcements. (EFCF 2026; Swiss Congress listing)

items.text: FuelCell Energy + Inuverse: 100 MW MCFC, Daegu, South Korea (first digest coverage): FCEL signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Inuverse for up to 100 MW of molten carbonate fuel cells at an AI-focused data center in Daegu, South Korea. Not SOFC, but marks FCEL's first announced Asian data center fuel cell deployment after pivoting from SOFC to MCFC. (FCEL press releases; Data Center Dynamics)
Confirmed SOFC pipeline (unchanged): Oracle 2.45 GW (NM), Project Jade/Google/Tallgrass 2.7 GW (WY), Nebius $2.6B, Brookfield $5B, AEP $2.65B, Equinix 100 MW+.

Germany EnEfG July 1 deadline: 10 days. New DCs commissioning from July 1 must achieve PUE ≤1.2 at commissioning and ERF ≥10% (rising to 15% in 2027, 20% in 2028); 100% renewable electricity from January 1, 2027. SOFC CHP waste heat qualifies for ERF ≥10%. No new guidance today. (Orrick: EnEfG draft amendment)
FERC RM26-4: RTOs have until ~mid-August 2026 to respond to Section 206 show-cause orders. Final tariff changes expected Q1 2027. SOFC BTM advantage intact. (FERC.gov)

Topsoe SOEC pullback (see Top Signals #1): Reduces European electrolyzer supply capacity for green H2 — broadly negative for long-term SOFC-H2 transition timeline, though near-term natural-gas-fueled SOFC is unaffected.

InterContinental Energy P2(H2)Node (see Top Signals #2): Competing off-grid model for Asia at claimed <$48/MWh via co-production of H2 and AI compute. Fundamentally different from dedicated SOFC BTM power delivery; relevant for SOFC positioning in Asian markets.
Quiet day. No new nuclear SMR, gas turbine, or battery announcements since June 19.

Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE): Holding ATH consolidation zone ~$328–330 on June 19 following ATH close of $329.51 on June 18. No new analyst actions today. Current targets: UBS Buy $322, Morgan Stanley OW $310, Bernstein MP $276. Manufacturing on track for 2 GW by end-2026.
Quiet day on FuelCell Energy (FCEL ~$17), Ceres Power (CWR:LON), Elcogen, Sunfire financial news.

lcoe.text: Topsoe SOEC pullback — Western H2 supply chain risk flag (NEW): Topsoe hibernating Herning + cancelling Chesterfield US plant reduces Western SOEC capacity. Prior digest established Western electrolyzer CAPEX at $700–1,000/kW vs. Chinese $300–450/kW. Topsoe's exit concentrates European SOEC development in Sunfire and smaller players. For SOFC LCOE H2-transition scenarios: add 2–3 additional years of supply chain delay risk vs. prior baseline for European deployments; Chinese SOEC trajectory unchanged. (Topsoe; QC Intel)

InterContinental Energy $48/MWh benchmark (NEW — requires interpretation): ICE's <$48/MWh AI compute power is achieved by co-producing 800 MW of H2 alongside 200 MW of data center capacity, netting H2 revenues against power costs. Not a standalone power generation LCOE and not directly comparable to SOFC ($125–200/MWh unsubsidized). Relevant for competitive benchmarking in Asian markets with strong H2 offtake; less applicable for European/US SOFC BTM deployments. (ICE; Hydrocarbon Processing)

Henry Hub (unchanged from June 19 digest): Q2 2026 spot ~$2.92/MMBtu; 2H26 forecast $3.34/MMBtu; FY2026 avg $3.60/MMBtu (EIA June 16 STEO). At current spot, SOFC fuel input ≈ $0.028–$0.034/kWh. No new weekly data today; EIA publishes Thursday.
